title: China, Nepal race to find thousands still missing 12 days after floods - Al Jazeera
description: China, Nepal race to find thousands still missing 12 days after floods  Al Jazeera

full_article:
Rescuers in Nepal are racing to reach thousands of people missing in areas near the China border after catastrophic floods as search operations enter their 12th day.

The flooding that authorities say was likely caused by a glacial collapse last month has killed at least 1,384 people and left more than 5,500 missing, among them about 800 foreigners, across the two countries.

Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Families perform symbolic funerals for missing Nepal flood victims

Families perform symbolic funerals for missing Nepal flood victims list 2 of 3 Stranded survivors in Nepal cross raging Trishuli River using zip line

Stranded survivors in Nepal cross raging Trishuli River using zip line list 3 of 3 Is Nepal leading the battle for climate justice? end of list

In Nepal, rescuers have retrieved 1,341 bodies and are searching for about 4,996 people, the national disaster agency said on Sunday. In Tibet, the death toll has risen to 43, with 519 people missing, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.

Four people have been found alive since Friday, three of them in tunnels at hydropower facilities, where the government initially said about 100 people could be alive. Nepal’s Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said teams at flooded hydropower tunnels were facing multiple challenges.

“Search and rescue is going on at the tunnels despite geography, adverse weather and lack of connectivity,” he told the AFP news agency.

On the Chinese side, rescuers face deep mud, poor weather and the risk of further landslides that have slowed work in the narrow gorge.

Nothing remains of a five-storey customs building at Gyirong, once China’s main land port with Nepal, where workers are digging with shovels, excavators and ground-penetrating radar to recover lost people.

The only road into Gyirong reopened on Wednesday, allowing heavy equipment in.

A case of climate justice

Nepal has issued a request that an untested climate emergency mechanism provide aid.

Advertisement

It is asking the United Nations-backed Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage – founded in 2022 to assist developing countries “particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change” – to cover some of the staggering costs of the flood.

The United Nations has appealed for $50m to help more than 84,000 people, saying the destruction makes delivering aid an immense challenge.

On Wednesday, Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal pointed to the role of leading greenhouse gas emitters that have a “historical responsibility to compensate vulnerable nations like Nepal”.

He added that the government has officially filed a “formal climate compensation claim letter” to international partners.

While the exact cause of the glacial collapse remains under investigation, experts say that the frequency and scale of glacier floods have increased as global temperatures have risen.

A United Nations study found that such floods have become nearly five times more frequent since 1950.

Manjeet Dhakal, lead adviser to the UN Least Developed Countries Group on Climate Change, says the global community has a responsibility to cover the cost of disasters afflicting developing nations like Nepal, and that the fund should accept the request.

Countries hit by such disasters are being forced to divert money set aside for health, education and development, he told Al Jazeera. “There are many cases where vulnerable countries are bearing their own cost,” Dhakal said.

The flood was “not caused because of what Nepal has done in the past or in current form”, Dhakal said, noting, “That’s where the global community has a bigger responsibility to come in.”

The UN fund has limited resources, he said. Indeed, its website reflects that it has received only about $631m of $822m in funds pledged by contributing states since inception, and has yet to spend out of the amount.

But, Dhakal said, even a “symbolic amount” could serve as an “inspiring lesson for the fund to justify what it was established for”.

A flood of emotion

Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque, reporting from a Buddhist monastery turned shelter in Kathmandu, said refugees there are still only just beginning to reckon with the trauma of the catastrophe.

“There are people meditating, praying, and there are children. It looks like there is a semblance of normal life,” Haque said. “But make no mistake, I was talking to some of the children here. They’ve lost everything. They’ve lost their families, their homes, their parents.”

About 200 people were brought by helicopter to the holy site, known as the Yellow Monastery, where doctors and volunteers have attended to them.

Advertisement

Haque spoke to a volunteer who had put out drawings for children to express their feelings.

“All of them put their stickers on ‘happy’, he said. Now why is that? The reason, he said, is that the children’s emotions remain suppressed so soon after the crisis,” Haque noted.

“What this volunteer told me is that in the days, months, or years to come, the floods will open, just like the floods open in the Himalayas, and emotions will be poured out.”

नेपालमे बचावकर्मी १,३४१ शव बरामद कए लगभग ४,९९६ गोटेके खोजमे लागल राष्ट्रिय आपदा एजेन्सी रविदिन जनौलक अछि । चीन के सरकारी समाचार एजेंसी सिन्हुआ के रिपोर्ट के अनुसार तिब्बत में मृतक के संख्या 43 भ गेल अछि, जाहि में 519 लोक लापता अछि।

नेपाल के साथ कहियो चीन के मुख्य स्थल बंदरगाह ग्यरोंग में पांच मंजिला सीमा शुल्क भवन के किछ नै बचल अछि, जतय मजदूर फावड़ा, खुदाई आ जमीन में घुसय वाला रडार सं खोद क हेरायल लोक के बरामद क रहल छथिन्ह.

बुधदिन ग्यरोंग मे प्रवेश करय वाला एकमात्र सड़क फेर सं खुलल, जाहि सं भारी उपकरण के अंदर घुसय के मौका मिलल.

जलवायु न्याय के एक मामला

नेपाल एकटा अपरीक्षित जलवायु आपातकालीन तंत्र स सहायता प्रदान करबाक आग्रह जारी केलक अछि ।

विज्ञापन

ई संयुक्त राष्ट्र समर्थित फंड फॉर रिस्पांडिंग टू लॉस एंड डेमेज स॑ कहै छै – जेकरऽ स्थापना २०२२ म॑ “जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ प्रतिकूल प्रभाव स॑ विशेष रूप स॑ कमजोर” विकासशील देशऽ क॑ मदद करै लेली करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै – ताकि बाढ़ केरऽ कुछ डगमगाबै वाला लागत क॑ पूरा करलऽ जाय ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र न॑ ८४ हजार स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मदद लेली ५० मिलियन डॉलर के अपील करलकै आरू कहलकै कि ई तबाही स॑ सहायता पहुँचैना एगो अपार चुनौती बनी गेलऽ छै ।

बुधदिन नेपाल के विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जक के अग्रणी के भूमिका दिस इशारा केलखिन्ह जेकरा पर “नेपाल सन कमजोर राष्ट्र के मुआवजा देबय के ऐतिहासिक जिम्मेदारी” अछि.

हुनी आरू कहलकै कि सरकार नँ आधिकारिक तौर प अंतरराष्ट्रीय भागीदारौ क “औपचारिक जलवायु मुआवजा दावा पत्र” दाखिल करलकै ।

हिमनदी केरऽ पतन केरऽ सही कारण केरऽ जांच जारी छै, लेकिन विशेषज्ञऽ के कहना छै कि वैश्विक तापमान बढ़ला के साथ ही ग्लेशियर केरऽ बाढ़ केरऽ आवृत्ति आरू पैमाना बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ एगो अध्ययन म॑ पता चललै कि 1950 स॑ ही ऐसनऽ बाढ़ लगभग पांच गुना अधिक होय गेलऽ छै ।

जलवायु परिवर्तन पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ अल्पविकसित देश समूह केरऽ प्रमुख सलाहकार मंजीत ढकाल के कहना छै कि नेपाल जैसनऽ विकासशील देशऽ क॑ परेशान करै वाला आपदा केरऽ खर्च पूरा करै के जिम्मेदारी वैश्विक समुदाय के छै, आरू कोष क॑ ई आग्रह क॑ स्वीकार करना चाहियऽ ।

अल जजीरा स॑ बातचीत म॑ हुनी कहलकै कि ऐसनऽ आपदा स॑ प्रभावित देशऽ क॑ स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा आरू विकास लेली अलग करलऽ गेलऽ पैसा क॑ मोड़ै लेली मजबूर करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । ढकल कहलनि जे, बहुत एहन मामला अछि जतय कमजोर देश अपन खर्चा उठा रहल अछि।

बाढ़ि “नेपाल पहिने जे काज केलक अछि या वर्तमान रूप मे केलक ओकर कारण नहि भेल”, ढकाल कहलनि, “ओतहि वैश्विक समुदाय के आबय के पैघ जिम्मेदारी अछि.”

ओ कहला जे संयुक्त राष्ट्र क कोष मे सीमित संसाधन अछि। दरअसल, एकरऽ वेबसाइट स॑ पता चलै छै कि ओकरा शुरू स॑ ही योगदान दै वाला राज्यऽ द्वारा प्रतिज्ञा करलऽ गेलऽ ८२२ मिलियन डॉलर केरऽ फंड म॑ स॑ मात्र लगभग ६३१ मिलियन डॉलर मिललऽ छै, आरू अभी तलक ओकरा ई राशि स॑ बाहर खर्च नै करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

लेकिन, ढकल न॑ कहलकै कि एगो “सांकेतिक राशि” भी “कोष लेली एगो प्रेरणादायक पाठ के रूप म॑ काम करी सकै छै कि ई कोष क॑ जायज ठहराबै के काम करलऽ जाय कि ओकरऽ स्थापना की लेली करलऽ गेलऽ छै” ।

भावुक बाढ़ि

काठमांडू केरऽ बौद्ध मठ स॑ आश्रय देलऽ गेलऽ अल जजीरा केरऽ निकोलस हक न॑ कहलकै कि वहाँ के शरणार्थी अभी भी प्रलय केरऽ आघात के हिसाब लगाना शुरू करी रहलऽ छै ।

हक कहलनि जे, लोक ध्यान करैत छथि, प्रार्थना करैत छथि, आ बच्चा सेहो अछि, लगैत अछि जेना सामान्य जीवनक आभास अछि। “मुदा गलती नहि करू, हम एत’क किछु बच्चा सभ सँ गप्प क’ रहल छलहुँ, सब किछु गमा लेलक, परिवार, घर, माता-पिता केँ गमा लेलक।”

लगभग 200 लोगऽ क॑ हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ ई पवित्र स्थल प॑ लानलऽ गेलै, जेकरा पीला मठ के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै, जहां डॉक्टर आरू स्वयंसेवक न॑ हुनकऽ देखभाल करी चुकलऽ छै ।

विज्ञापन

हक एकटा स्वयंसेवक स गप केलथि जे बच्चा सब लेल ड्राइंग लगा क अपन भावना व्यक्त केने छलाह।

ओ कहलनि जे, सब अपन स्टिकर ‘हैप्पी’ पर लगा देलनि। आब से किएक? हुनकऽ कहना छै कि एकरऽ कारण ई छै कि संकट के बाद भी बच्चा सिनी के भावना एतना जल्दी दबाय देलऽ जाय छै,’’ हक न॑ नोट करलकै ।

“ई स्वयंसेवक हमरा जे कहलक से ई जे आबै बला दिन, महीना, वा साल मे बाढ़ि खुजत, ठीक ओहिना जेना हिमालय मे बाढ़ि खुजत, आ भाव उझलि जायत।”

publisher.title: TRT World
full_article:
The death toll from devastating flash floods in Nepal has reached at least 1,342, with thousands still missing, officials and local media reports have said.

The combined death toll from flash floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border rose to at least 1,385, while 5,519 people remained missing 11 days after the disaster struck, according to official data from the two countries on Sunday.

Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said around 5,000 people, including 589 foreigners, remained missing.

More than 13,000 people have so far been rescued from the flood-hit areas.

Chinese authorities said at least 43 people have been confirmed dead, while 519 others remained missing in Tibet.

Of those missing, 850 are foreigners, according to official figures from Nepal and China.

Related TRT World - Rescuers pull Chinese national alive from Nepal tunnel after 10 days

‘We are not getting enough to eat’

With roads and bridges damaged due to massive floods and landslides, thousands of expectant and new mothers are struggling hardest to find a female-friendly space to breastfeed, get proper food and reach emergency care if labour turns dangerous, the local English daily Kathmandu Post reported.

The mothers also complain about cigarette smoke, the smell of alcohol and, on top of all that, unhygienic food and water, which upset their and their babies' stomachs.

Also, there are no vaccination facilities for children in the shelter camps.

"We are not getting food on time either. We are not getting enough to eat,” a new mother who wished to be identified only as Pariyar said.

Pariyar fled her home when floods struck her hometown, Trishuli, on the morning of August 26 and is now staying with dozens of strangers under one roof in a shelter camp.

title: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel - kmph.com
description: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel  kmph.com
publisher.title: kmph.com
full_article:
(TNND) — Ten days after catastrophic flash floods tore through Nepal’s mountains, rescuers pulled a Chinese worker from a mud-filled hydropower tunnel, a rare moment of relief amid a disaster that has killed more than 1,300 people and left thousands unaccounted for.

The flash floods struck Nepal and China’s Tibet region on Aug. 26, likely after a glacier collapse. Nepal’s disaster management agency said nearly 4,900 people remain missing. Earlier in the response, authorities reported more than 3,700 people had been rescued in Nepal.

On the Tibet side of the border, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported 43 deaths and 519 people missing as of Saturday evening. CCTV said 261 of those missing were foreigners.

Rescue operations have focused in part on hydropower sites in Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the devastated Gyirong border crossing in Tibet. Authorities previously believed more than 100 people could be trapped inside a mud-filled tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project.

CCTV reported that Lu Haitao, a 49-year-old Chinese worker, was rescued Saturday from a 225-meter, or roughly 740-foot, hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa, 10 days after the floods. Rescuers carried Lu out of the tunnel and evacuated him by helicopter, according to CCTV, which reported he was hospitalized in stable condition.

Lu told CCTV he had climbed to the highest point in the tunnel and had begun to lose hope before rescue crews found him. CCTV reported Lu is a former farmer from Henan province who also worked as a carpenter, and that he traveled to Nepal in February for his first job abroad.

As the search continues, families of missing people have searched hospitals and relief centers and posted photographs and contact information in hopes of finding relatives.

Rescue work has been complicated by steep mountains, narrow gorges and concern about further flooding from a lake that formed in the Himalayas after the initial disaster. Chinese monitoring data showed the water level in that new lake had dropped about 10 meters, or 32 feet, from its peak.

Nepal said it mobilized domestic and international resources, including an 11-member tunnel-rescue reconnaissance team from India. A similar team from China was expected.

Nepal has received more than 57 metric tons of relief supplies from India, with aid also arriving from China, Japan, Australia and other countries.

The United Nations’ top official in Nepal has issued an emotional appeal for international aid, warning that survivors of the catastrophic Himalayan flooding last month saw their lives transformed “in one to two minutes”.

The UN Resident Coordinator, Lila Pieters Yahia, said communities along the China-Nepal border were struggling to comprehend the scale of devastation after torrential floods on August 26 tore through mountain districts, destroying roads, bridges and hydropower dams.

“You lose your home, you lose your livelihood, you lose your loved one and you lose the breadwinner of your family,” she told the AFP news agency in Kathmandu. “And you know, this happened in one to two minutes.”

At least 1,384 people were killed and more than 5,500 others remain missing in Nepal and the Tibet region of China. Among the missing are more than 800 foreigners from at least 34 countries, including tourists and pilgrims.

Many communities near the epicentre remain cut off, with roads washed away and journeys that once took hours now stretching into days. The UN, working with Nepal’s government, has launched a $50m appeal to support more than 84,000 people affected.

The UN’s Pieters Yahia warned of the risk of cholera and other communicable diseases, citing the deaths of 5,000 cattle and urging urgent investment in sanitation, hygiene and protection for vulnerable women and girls.

“My plea to the international community is: this is the time to help Nepal,” she said. “We can’t leave them alone.”

full_article:
Kathmandu, Sept. 6 (SANA) The death toll from devastating floods that struck mountain valleys in Nepal along the border with China has risen to at least 1,341, with nearly 5,000 people reported missing as search and rescue operations continue.

Citing a provisional tally released Sunday by Nepal‘s emergency response authority, Agence France-Presse reported that a wall of water, ice, and debris swept through northern valleys, leaving 1,341 dead and 4,996 missing. Those missing include hundreds of foreign tourists as well as approximately 900 workers stationed at power plants and dam sites at the time of the disaster.

Nepali Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha confirmed that rescue teams are working around the clock 11 days after the disaster struck. He noted that operations are currently focused on power project tunnels despite severe geographical obstacles, bad weather, and a total collapse of local communications.

Shrestha added that large helicopters can no longer land at two key sites to deliver heavy equipment, though teams are evaluating alternative methods to advance the operation. Rescue workers recently pulled three survivors from the Trishuli-3 dam project tunnels—two Nepali workers and a Chinese national—and rescued a woman in her 60s from a mud-buried home.

Preliminary official estimates place the economic damage to housing, infrastructure, and property at a minimum of 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees (approximately $2.56 billion). The disaster was triggered on Aug. 26 when flash floods, mudslides, and rockfalls swept through Himalayan border districts, severing roads, power supply, and communications.

नेपाल केरऽ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया प्राधिकरण द्वारा रविवार क॑ जारी करलऽ गेलऽ प्रोविजनल टैली के हवाला दैत॑ एजेंसी फ्रांस-प्रेस न॑ रिपोर्ट करलकै कि उत्तरी घाटी म॑ पानी, बर्फ आरू मलबा के देवाल बहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ १,३४१ लोगऽ के मौत आरू ४,९९६ लोगऽ के लापता होय गेलऽ छै । लापता लोगऽ म॑ सैकड़ों विदेशी पर्यटक के साथ-साथ आपदा के समय बिजली संयंत्र आरू बांध स्थल प॑ तैनात लगभग ९०० मजदूर भी शामिल छै ।

नेपाली ऊर्जा मन्त्री विराज भक्त श्रेष्ठ आपदा आएल ११ दिन बाद बचाव दल चौबीसों घंटा कार्यरत रहल पुष्टि केने छथि । हुनी नोट करलकै कि भारी भौगोलिक बाधा, खराब मौसम, आरू स्थानीय संचार केरौ कुल पतन के बावजूद अभी परिचालन बिजली परियोजना सुरंगौ प केंद्रित छै ।

श्रेष्ठ न॑ आरू कहलकै कि अब॑ बड़ऽ हेलीकॉप्टर भारी उपकरण पहुँचै लेली दू प्रमुख स्थल प॑ नै उतरी सकै छै, हालांकि टीम सब ऑपरेशन क॑ आगू बढ़ाबै लेली वैकल्पिक तरीका के मूल्यांकन करी रहलऽ छै । हाल ही म॑ बचावकर्मी न॑ त्रिशुली-३ बांध परियोजना केरऽ सुरंगऽ स॑ तीन बची गेलऽ लोगऽ क॑ खींच॑ लेलकै – दू नेपाली मजदूर आरू एक चीनी नागरिक – आरू ६० के दशक के एगो महिला क॑ थाल स॑ गाड़लऽ घर स॑ बचा लेलकै ।

प्रारंभिक आधिकारिक अनुमान के अनुसार आवास, बुनियादी ढांचा, आ संपत्ति के आर्थिक नुकसान न्यूनतम 387.5 अरब नेपाली रुपया (लगभग 2.56 अरब डॉलर) अछि. ई आपदा 26 अगस्त क॑ तखनिये शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै जब॑ हिमालय केरऽ सीमावर्ती जिला म॑ आकस्मिक बाढ़, कीचड़, आरू चट्टान गिरला स॑ सड़क, बिजली आपूर्ति, आरू संचार टूटी गेलऽ छेलै ।
